lines.text: His or her? Look at Anna!
Many learners say: Anna loves his job.
His is for a man. Her is for a woman.
His! My brother loves his job.

data.why: His is for a man. Her is for a woman.

native.tip: En français, « son » ne change pas selon la personne. En anglais, “his” = lui, “her” = elle : on regarde le possesseur.
native.caption: Vous dites “Anna loves his job.” ? En français, « son travail » ne change pas. En anglais, on choisit selon le possesseur : Anna = “her”, Ali = “his”. Dites plutôt “Anna loves her job.” — écoutez Ama et répétez avec elle ! Plus d’exercices dans l’appli Lexkite.
native.comment: Réponse : “Anna loves her job.” — En français, « son travail » ne change pas. En anglais, on choisit selon le possesseur : Anna = “her”, Ali = “his”. À vous : dites la phrase à voix haute, puis écrivez une phrase de votre cru. Quiz gratuit : {link}

en.hook: His or her? Look at the owner!
en.tip: French “son” fits both. English needs “his” or “her”.
en.caption: Do you say this? “Anna loves his job.” French “son” fits both. English needs “his” or “her”. Say “Anna loves her job.” Listen to Ama and repeat with her! More exercises in the Lexkite app.
